summary: Upper Klamath Refuge lookout: a 1935 Forest Service permit, a 1937 steel-tower move, a 1974 dismantling. Three foundation blocks remain (2015 visit); no public access.

facts.design: Steel tower (1937 newspaper item); the 1935 permit covered a tower and cabin
facts.status_note: Tower gone; three foundation blocks remain at the old refuge headquarters (2015 visit).

access.note: Signs at the compound entrances say No Public Access (2015 record). Wikipedia says the refuge is reached only by boat.

events.note: Forest Service special use permit (June 29, 1935) for a lookout tower and cabin supporting refuge administration; 30.05 acres of Forest Service land

Newspaper item (May 6, 1937): steel tower being dismantled at the Tule Lake biological survey headquarters for a move to the Upper Klamath Lake Preserve; completion of the move is not confirmed by the page
Dismantled by a crew from the Cave Junction Smoke Jumper base and transported to 'that site'; the entry does not name the destination
Site visit (May 2, 2015): three foundation blocks remain at the old refuge headquarters; No Public Access signs at compound entrances

evidence.supports: 1935 Forest Service special use permit for a lookout tower and cabin supporting refuge administration
evidence.quote: June 29, 1935: A Special use permit was issued by the Forest Service for the purpose of erecting a lookout tower and cabin in connection with the administration and supervision of Upper Klamath Lake Refuge.

evidence.supports: permit covered 30.05 acres of Forest Service land
evidence.quote: The area under the permit was 30.05 acres of Forest Service land.

evidence.supports: refuge set apart 7,560 acres in April 1928 by Calvin Coolidge, as a refuge for birds and wild animals
evidence.quote: On April 3, 1928, Calvin Coolidge reserved and set apart 7,560 acres of lands to be known as the Upper Klamath Wildlife Refuge, for the use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals

evidence.supports: refuge established 1928 and contains about 14,400 acres today
evidence.quote: It was established in 1928 and contains some 14,400 acres

evidence.supports: 1937 item: steel tower being dismantled at Tule Lake biological survey headquarters
evidence.quote: May 6, 1937: Workmen are shown dismantling the big steel tower at the biological survey headquarters on the west side of Tule Lake

evidence.supports: 1937 item: tower used by game agents to watch for poachers and to be moved to the Upper Klamath Lake Preserve
evidence.quote: this tower, which was used by game agents to watch for poachers on the bird reserve, will be moved to the Upper Klamath Lake Preserve and utilized there for the same purpose.

evidence.supports: 1974 dismantling by Cave Junction smokejumper base crew, transported to that site
evidence.quote: 1974: The tower was dismantled by a crew from the Cave Junction Smoke Jumper base and transported to that site.

evidence.supports: 2015: tower site at old refuge headquarters; three foundation blocks; nothing else remains
evidence.quote: The lookout site consists of three foundation blocks, the fourth and a possible step pad are either buried or removed, nothing else remains.

evidence.supports: 2015: tower site located at the old refuge headquarters
evidence.quote: May 2, 2015: The tower site is located at the old Upper Klamath Refuge headquarters.

evidence.supports: 2015: No Public Access signs at compound entrances
evidence.quote: Signs posted at the entrances to the compound point out "No Public Access".

evidence.supports: refuge reached only by boat from Rocky Point, Malone Springs and neighboring ramps
evidence.quote: It is accessible only by boat from Rocky Point Resort and Rocky Point boat launch, Malone springs, and a few neighboring ramps

notes_for_editor: The 1935 permit and the 1937 steel-tower move may not refer to the same structure, and the page does not say when a tower was first erected at the refuge, so no built event is recorded. The 1974 entry says the tower went to 'that site' without naming it; the story says so. Acreage conflict: the FWS page gives 7,560 acres reserved in 1928, Wikipedia gives about 14,400 acres now; no source we read explains the change. The 'No Public Access' sign and the site description are from a 2015 visit; check current signage before any visit. Searches for other sources on a Tule Lake or Upper Klamath tower, and for the Crater National Forest permit, found nothing further. Brief record had status and access unknown; set to ruins and closed from the 2015 record.
